$comment: TEAM A / PHASE A - THE FROZEN SHAPE OF A PER-CRAWL EGRESS FENCE.
THE DEFECT THIS CLOSES (R2 / G2). The squid allowlist was ONE FILE PER
WORKER: qe-central wrote allowed_domains.txt, squid matched a single
dstdomain ACL against it for every request. At capacity > 1 the second
crawl dispatched to a worker overwrote the first crawl's live fence - a
cross-tenant egress leak, recorded by the strict xfail in
tests/fleet/test_t_fl_08_concurrency_redteam.py and made unreachable only
by the admission clamp (FENCE_IS_PER_WORKER). The ARB record
(QECentral/docs/ARB_EGRESS_FENCE_DECISION.md) is right that per-crawl FILES
alone fix nothing: squid must SELECT the fence per crawl, which needs a
per-request identity. That identity is the PROXY LOGIN.
THE MECHANISM, across three parties that cannot share a test process:
qe-central   routers/explorations._write_egress_allowlist(domains, allowlist_path, crawl_id=...)
writes  <root>/crawls/allowlist.<crawl_id>.txt   (one dstdomain file per crawl)
regenerates <root>/crawls.conf                   (one ACL pair + one allow per live crawl)
rewrites <root>/reload.stamp                     (content changes -> squid is HUP'd)
squid        engines/qe-explorer/squid.conf
include /etc/squid/allowlist/crawls.conf; every crawl must authenticate to the
proxy (basic_fake_auth accepts any password; the USERNAME is the crawl id), and the
http_access line for crawl X allows ONLY the fence of X. Unauthenticated -> 407.
Authenticated to a foreign host -> 403. No shared file is consulted at all.
qe-explorer  app/fence.py -> the browser CONTEXT for crawl X is created with proxy credentials
username = X, so every request the crawl makes carries its own identity.
<root> is the DIRECTORY of the worker's registered allowlist_path (qec_022
column): qe-central sees it at /qec/egress-allowlist, squid at
/etc/squid/allowlist - the same volume. Two workers registering the same
allowlist_path still share a root and are still refused together (T-FL-04
fence_conflicts): the per-crawl fence isolates crawls WITHIN a worker; the
per-worker root isolates workers.
FAIL-CLOSED BY CONSTRUCTION. A crawl whose file was never written has no ACL
line and reaches nothing. A browser context without credentials is 407'd and
reaches nothing. A missing crawls.conf is seeded EMPTY by the proxy's
entrypoint, which is deny-all. An old explorer image (no credentials) against
the new squid.conf reaches nothing - the safe direction for a mixed deploy.
CHANGING THIS FILE IS A PROTOCOL CHANGE across three deployables. Bump
schema_version and add the new version beside this one.

roots.$comment: Derived at runtime as dirname(allowlist_path); these literals are the shipped compose values and what the tests assert the shipped squid.conf uses.

proxy_identity.$comment: basic_fake_auth accepts any password; the username is the whole identity. The password is a constant, NOT a secret, and is documented as such - a per-crawl secret would be theatre while the helper does not verify it.

tag_rule: crawl_id with every character outside [A-Za-z0-9] replaced by underscore

sample.per_crawl_file_body:
# fence for crawl 9c21b4e0a1b2c3d4e5f60718293a4b5c (written by qe-central at dispatch, fail-closed)
.acmelife.example
